description.narrative: Renewed fighting and violence since early December 25 have exacerbated the humanitarian situation in DRC. Even prior to the currentescalation, the country was facing a severe humanitarian crisis: 27.7 million ppl were food insecure, with eastern provinces more affected. Nationwide outbreaks included more than 10k cholera cases, over 8,900 Mpox cases, <(>&<)> 64 Ebola cases reported in 2025 (WHO). According to UN Flash Updates (12–19 December 2025), renewed fighting has resulted in displacement of over 500,000 people across South Kivu. RNA <(>&<)> inter-agency missions conducted indicate that more than 95% of IDPs arrived without food stocks. Access to safe drinking water is critically limited, forcing families to rely on untreated river or canal water. Oxfam’s RNA identified WASH, FSL, Health, <(>&<)> Protection as first-priority needs in Uvira during current phase of crisis. While some actors are providing essential health <(>&<)> water services in selected locations, overall coverage remains insufficient, with critical gaps in WASH and Food security. To address these gaps, Oxfam <(>&<)> AFEDEM will conduct an integrated WASH <(>&<)> FSL response in Uvira, with gender <(>&<)> protection mainstreaming. The intervention will adhere to Sphere <(>&<)> cluster standards, target 15,750 ppl, strengthen JR synergies, <(>&<)> remain relevant should displacement dynamics shift towards returns.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
